summary: TestUUIDPathOperationsDeclareBadRequest closes only the path-param subset — body/query/header 400 sources are still unguarded (TKT-110 follow-up)
description:
### Incidental finding spun out of TKT-110 (agent's own post-review verification, not the ai-review)

TKT-110 added `TestUUIDPathOperationsDeclareBadRequest`
(`services/catalog/internal/api/lifecycle_badrequest_test.go`), which closes a *class*: every catalog
operation with a `format: uuid` **path** parameter must declare `'400'`, because the oapi-codegen
binder can always reject one.

**That is one subset of the class, not the class.** The generated binder and the kin-openapi request
validator can also emit a 400 from:

- a **required `requestBody`** that is absent or schema-invalid (measured on TKT-110: invalid JSON,
  wrong property type, `minLength` violation, and a wrong `Content-Type` all produce 400 from the
  request validator),
- a **query parameter** that fails to bind or violates its schema,
- a **required header** parameter, same.

`getOpenAPISpec` is correctly outside this (it is served before validation).

**No current gap** — verified at TKT-110's merge: every catalog operation with a request body or a
constrained query/header parameter already declares `'400'`, and the nine that did not have one now do.
So this is latent, not live. But the invariant test's name and failure message speak only of path
parameters, and a future operation with a required body and no uuid path parameter would slip through
exactly the way these nine did — which is the failure mode ADR-028's corrected Consequences now
describe: *any status the binder or the request validator can write must be declared.*

**Scope to settle at plan time**

- [ ] Broaden the invariant to every rejection source the request layer has, or add a second invariant
      test per source — decide which reads better as a failure message
- [ ] Decide whether the same invariant belongs in the four non-codegen services. Their request
      validator does **not** reject malformed UUIDs today (`format: uuid` is unenforced repo-wide — no
      `EnableFormatValidation` / `DefineStringFormat` call exists), and their hand-rolled `parseUUID`
      400s *are* declared, so the answer may legitimately be no
- [ ] Related but separable: whether to enable `openapi3.EnableFormatValidation` at all. TKT-110
      explicitly rejected it as out of scope — it changes request-validation behaviour on every
      operation in all five services and could turn currently-succeeding requests into 400s. If that
      is ever adopted, this invariant's shape changes, so sequence them

**Governing:** ADR-028 (fail-closed on undeclared statuses, and its TKT-110 correction that the
carve-out does not hold for catalog), ADR-009 (spec is authoritative; any spec change ⇒ regen).

**Not urgent.** Nothing is broken today; this raises the ceiling on a test that currently prevents a
recurrence of nine real production defects.

governingAdrs.why: Its TKT-110-corrected Consequences state the rule this ticket would enforce more completely: for catalog, any status the binder or request validator can write must be declared, because response validation is the outermost wrap.
Spec-authoritative: if the outcome adds declarations, `make generate` runs and the regen is committed before the gate.

reference.summary: The test to broaden, and TKT-110's measurements of every 400 source it does not yet cover.
Source ticket with the full probe evidence (binder vs request validator, and why format:uuid is unenforced).

### ✅ Implementation readiness — PASS

All 8 items `met`. Ran the widened predicate over `services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml` at HEAD rather than inheriting TKT-110's merge-time verification:

> **live gaps: 0** — every catalog operation with a `requestBody` or a constrained query/header parameter already declares `'400'`.

So the ticket is still latent, which is the clean case: pure invariant-widening, no spec fix riding along.

**The one hard part is the proof, and it is called out in `success`.** A coverage ticket with no live defect cannot use red-then-green. The demonstration that works is a temporary spec mutation — remove a `'400'` from one body-bearing operation, show the **widened** test catches it and the **current** test does not, revert. Two runs. Without that comparison, "we widened the class" is exactly the unfalsifiable claim AGENTS.md warns about.

Three pieces of the existing test must survive the widening: the `Responses.Default()` arm (a `default:` response legitimately satisfies the invariant under kin-openapi), the deliberate absence of the hand-mounted `/internal/*` chi routes from the document, and the `getOpenAPISpec` exclusion. And widen the **failure message** too — it currently explains uuid path parameters, and a message that misstates why an operation owes a 400 aims the next reader at the wrong fix.

**Risk verdict — `risk:low` NOT claimed.**

By blast radius it would qualify: one test file, no production code, no auth/money/migration/CI surface. But the label is about blast radius *and* the ticket's central question, and this ticket's central question is precisely the shape the invariant carves out: **"how do I construct a proof that can actually fail?"** It is a coverage ticket with **zero live gaps** — the readiness item ran the widened predicate over `services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml` at HEAD and found none — so red-then-green is unavailable, and "we widened the class" is unfalsifiable without a deliberate spec mutation demonstrating that the widened predicate catches what the current one misses. comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
### Plan draft — by `gpt-5.6-luna` (codex `task`, effort high)

Rung 1, one attempt, 7538 bytes, conclusive. The run showed the known local-skill hijack (it read `~/.ai/skills/unslop/SKILL.md`) — survivable per `codex-runner.md`, and it returned concrete, code-cited findings, so it is a pass. Verbatim below; my critique follows as `kind=plan-final`.

---

# DoD

- `services/catalog/internal/api/lifecycle_badrequest_test.go` checks every documented catalog operation with a request-layer 400 source.
- The test still accepts either an explicit `'400'` response or `default:`.
- `getOpenAPISpec` passes without a name-based exclusion.
- The test name and failure message no longer describe only UUID path parameters.
- The sibling runtime test remains valid and unchanged in behavior.
- Temporary mutations are reverted. `make check` passes with no generated-file or OpenAPI drift.
- Mutation evidence is recorded in the TKT-142 execution notes or PR description.

# Files touched

Final change:

- [services/catalog/internal/api/lifecycle_badrequest_test.go](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/catalog/internal/api/lifecycle_badrequest_test.go:57)

Temporary proof mutation only, restored before completion:

- [services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml:51)
- [services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml:1049)

No production code, generated code, ADR, or OpenAPI change remains.

# Design

Rename `TestUUIDPathOperationsDeclareBadRequest` to:

```go
TestCatalogRequestRejectionSourcesDeclareBadRequest
```

Replace the UUID-only predicate with a predicate covering these sources:

```text
format: uuid path parameter
declared requestBody
query parameter
header parameter
```

The predicate should inspect both path-item and operation parameters, preserving the existing `item.Parameters` plus `op.Parameters` traversal. `$ref`s are already resolved by `openapi3.NewLoader().LoadFromData`, but each parameter reference should still be skipped when `ref.Value == nil`.

Use the following rules:

- A path parameter counts only when `in: path` and its schema format is `"uuid"`. Do not broaden this to every path parameter.
- Any non-nil, resolved `op.RequestBody` counts, regardless of `required`. A required body can be absent, and an optional body can still be schema-invalid when supplied.
- Any parameter with `in: query` or `in: header` counts. Missing required parameters, binding failures, and supplied values that violate the parameter schema can all produce 400.
- Keep the response check exactly as it is:

```go
op.Responses.Value("400") == nil && op.Responses.Default() == nil
```

The `Default()` arm is required because kin-openapi treats `default:` as matching 400.

The failure should describe the actual class, for example:

```text
operations with a catalog request-layer rejection source
(format:uuid path, request body, query, or header) can return 400;
ADR-028 turns an undeclared 400 into 500, so each must declare
'400' or 'default'. Missing on ...
```

Update the surrounding comments in the file so they explain the broader invariant. Keep the existing runtime test, `TestLifecycleRejectionsAreDeclaredBadRequests`, unchanged in its request coverage. It already proves the real 400 behavior for malformed UUID binding and an invalid request body. The widened test is a spec-level class check, not a replacement for those runtime assertions.

The two documented internal operations are in scope because they are generated routes present in `doc.Paths.Map()`:

- `resolvePerformanceDisplayNames` has required query parameters at [openapi.yaml:1037](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml:1037).
- `resolveTicketTypeFees` has a UUID path parameter and query parameter at [openapi.yaml:1103](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml:1103).

The other hand-mounted `/internal/*` routes are absent from the OpenAPI document and therefore correctly outside this spec traversal. `getOpenAPISpec` is also excluded structurally because it has no parameters or request body. Do not add a name-based exception.

# Test plan / proof of the gap

Use two temporary mutations because body and query are distinct newly-covered source branches. Both selected operations have no UUID path parameter, so the old test cannot catch either mutation.

Run each mutation separately, with no gate or generator running.

| Mutation | Why it proves the gap |
|---|---|
| Remove the `'400'` response from `POST /venues`, operation `createVenue`, at [openapi.yaml:51](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml:51) | Required request body, no path parameters |
| Remove the `'400'` response from `GET /internal/performances/display-names`, operation `resolvePerformanceDisplayNames`, at [openapi.yaml:1049](/home/mathieu/sources/ticketing_system/services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml:1049) | Required query parameters, no UUID path parameter |

For each mutation:

1. Run the current test before changing the test implementation:

   ```sh
   cd services/catalog
   go test -count=1 ./internal/api \
     -run '^TestUUIDPathOperationsDeclareBadRequest$'
   ```

   Expected result: pass. The old predicate does not inspect the selected body or query source.

2. Apply the widened test implementation and run:

   ```sh
   go test -count=1 ./internal/api \
     -run '^TestCatalogRequestRejectionSourcesDeclareBadRequest$'
   ```

   Expected result: fail and identify the mutated operation, such as:

   ```text
   Missing on 1:
     post /venues (createVenue)
   ```

3. Restore the exact `'400'` line before starting the next mutation.

4. Record both results, including the command, mutation, and expected pass/fail, in the TKT-142 execution notes or PR description.

The temporary change only affects the embedded `services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml` read by `services/catalog/api/spec.go`. Do not run `make generate` while the temporary response is removed, and do not leave any generated output from the experiment. Verify that the temporary OpenAPI diff is empty before the final gate.

After restoring the spec:

```sh
cd services/catalog
go test -count=1 ./internal/api \
  -run '^TestCatalogRequestRejectionSourcesDeclareBadRequest$'
go test -count=1 ./internal/api \
  -run '^TestLifecycleRejectionsAreDeclaredBadRequests$'
cd ../..
make check
```

# Risks

- Counting only `required: true` request bodies would miss malformed optional bodies such as `closeSlot`. Count every resolved request body.
- Counting only operation-level parameters would miss path-item parameters. Preserve both parameter sets.
- Counting every path parameter would expand the invariant beyond the stated UUID binder guarantee and may create false positives.
- A future optional query or header parameter still belongs in the predicate because an invalid supplied value can be rejected with 400.
- The current specification has no header parameters, so the header branch has no live mutation proof. The implementation must still include it for future operations.
- Removing a response from the temporary spec while running `make generate` or `make check` could create misleading generated drift. Keep the mutation isolated, restore it, then run the gate.
- The invariant checks declaration coverage, not every runtime rejection path. That is appropriate here because the existing sibling test already exercises representative runtime behavior.

# Open decisions

None. The settled scope supports one final test-file change, with body and query mutations used to prove that the widened predicate catches gaps invisible to the current UUID-only predicate.

objective.note: TestUUIDPathOperationsDeclareBadRequest closes a CLASS by design — that is its stated point and why it is spec-only. But the class it actually closes is narrower than the class that exists: the binder and the kin-openapi request validator also emit 400 from a required requestBody, a constrained query parameter and a required header. A future operation with a body and no uuid path parameter slips through exactly the way the nine that TKT-110 fixed did, and under ADR-028 an undeclared 400 becomes a 500.

scope.note: IN: services/catalog/internal/api/lifecycle_badrequest_test.go — widen the predicate from 'has a format:uuid path parameter' to the full set of binder/validator 400 sources, and correct the test name and failure message, which today speak only of path parameters. OUT: fixing catalog operations (there are none to fix — see uncertainties). OUT: the other four services, which have their own specs and their own version of this test or none; TKT-256 is already handling payments' sibling shape for 500.

uncertainties.note: The load-bearing one — 'is this still latent, or has a live gap appeared since TKT-110 merged?' — was settled by running the widened predicate over the spec at HEAD rather than trusting the ticket's 'verified at TKT-110's merge'. Result: **zero** live gaps. Every catalog operation with a requestBody or a constrained query/header parameter already declares '400'. So this ticket is pure invariant-widening with no accompanying spec fix, which is the clean case. Second, smaller: `getOpenAPISpec` is correctly outside the class (served before validation) and the hand-mounted /internal/* chi routes are absent from the document entirely — both already handled by the existing test's structure, both must survive the widening.

dependencies.note: None. No blockers. TKT-110 (the origin) is Done.

approach.note: Verified against the test at HEAD before inheriting the ticket's framing. The existing test is already the right shape — spec-only, drives no requests, covers operation number ten without a fixture — so this is a predicate widening inside a good structure, not a rewrite. Three details the drafter must preserve: (1) the `op.Responses.Default() == nil` arm, which is there because a `default:` response satisfies 400 under kin-openapi's status matching and without it a contract-correct future operation fails; (2) the deliberate absence of the /internal/* chi routes from the document; (3) the exclusion of `getOpenAPISpec`. The failure message must be widened too — it currently explains the uuid-path-parameter reasoning, and a message that misstates WHY an operation owes a 400 sends the next reader to the wrong fix.

first_slice.note: The whole ticket is one slice — one predicate, one name, one message. The four 400 sources could be added one at a time but there is no reason to: they share the predicate's structure and the spec has no live gap for any of them.

success.note: **This is the item that needs the most care, because the ticket is a coverage ticket with no live defect — so the ordinary proof (the test goes red, then the fix makes it green) is unavailable.** AGENTS.md's rule still applies: demonstrate the gap. The honest demonstration here is a temporary spec mutation — add or take a body/query-parameter 400 off one operation, show the widened test catches it and the CURRENT test does not, then revert. That two-run comparison IS the deliverable's evidence; without it 'we widened the invariant' is unfalsifiable, and per AGENTS.md a green test that cannot reach the failing state looks exactly like one that proves something. Then: the test name and message speak of the real class, no live gap is introduced, `make check` green.

context_memo.note: governingAdrs (resolve at HEAD): ADR-028 (docs/adr/ADR-028-response-drift-fail-closed.md) — the fail-closed validation that turns an undeclared 400 into a 500, i.e. the entire reason this invariant is worth having; ADR-009 (docs/adr/ADR-009-contract-first-apis.md) — contract-first and the regen-before-gate rule, relevant only if a spec line is touched. governingTests: services/catalog/internal/api/lifecycle_badrequest_test.go — the subject itself, whose `hasUUIDPathParam` helper and `default:` arm carry the reasoning above. Sibling worth reading, not editing: TKT-256 is widening the same invariant shape for 500 in payments; if both land, the two tests should be recognisable as the same pattern.
